functions.name: answer-questions
functions.description: Evaluate named yes/no, choice, and rubric-score questions against shared content and return probabilities without inventing certainty.

type.description: Ask for probability of yes/true rather than a forced boolean.

yesCriteria.description: Optional definition of yes; null means unspecified.

anyOf.description: A yes/no question answered with a probability.

type.description: Select among named options and report their probabilities.

additionalProperties.description: Option description, or null to use its name alone.

options.description: Option names mapped to descriptions; null lets an option name speak for itself.

anyOf.description: A question selecting among named options.

type.description: Rate against ordered zero-based rubric levels.

items.description: Description of this zero-based rubric level.

levels.description: Ordered rubric descriptions; each array index is that level's numeric score.

instructions.description: Optional description of what to rate.

anyOf.description: A question evaluating an ordered rubric.

additionalProperties.description: A named yes/no, choice, or rubric-score question.

questions.description: Named decision questions; keys correlate answers.

FunctionInput_perplexity_answerquestions.description: A decision model, shared content, and up to 128 named questions.

model.description: Model name echoed by provider; an alias is not a resolved immutable model version.

usage.description: Token counts for the decision computation.

type.description: Probability answer to a yes/no question.

probabilityYes.description: Probability of yes/true; near 0.5 indicates uncertainty.

confidence.description: Provider confidence relative to an equal-probability baseline; not probability of correctness.

probabilities.description: Probability per option; sums approximately to one.

anyOf.description: A selected option and its probability distribution.

score.description: Probability-weighted mean of zero-based level indices; may be fractional.

additionalProperties.description: Rubric description for this level index.

legend.description: Stringified level indices mapped to their rubric descriptions.

confidence.description: Provider spread-based rubric confidence, not probability of correctness.

probabilities.description: Probability per stringified level index; sums approximately to one.

anyOf.description: An expected rubric score and its probability distribution.

additionalProperties.description: The answer to this named question.

answers.description: Answer keyed by exactly the supplied question names.

tags.instructions: Use for classification or scoring of supplied content, not open-ended research. Define up to 128 named questions; answers retain those names. yesNo returns a probability, not a boolean; score can fall between levels. Body must be under 32 MiB and state plus each question under 256K input tokens. Aliases can change model version over time.

FunctionInput_perplexity_batchcreateagen.description: Submit typed Agent requests with a shared model, or an existing batch input file.

id.description: Batch job ID for progress and cancellation.

This returns a job, not per-request success. Use `get-batch` for progress, `download-batch-file` for output/error files, and `cancel-batch` to stop outstanding work. Results can take hours and are retained 30 days. Use `create-agent-response` for a single interactive task.

functions.name: cancel-agent-response

tags.instructions: Use an ID from `create-agent-response` or `get-agent-response`. Cancellation stops ongoing work asynchronously and does not undo work already performed. After acknowledgment use `get-agent-response` to see the terminal state. An already-terminal response cannot be cancelled.

Use `get-batch` for the final state and result files. Finalizing, completed, expired, and failed batches cannot be cancelled.
